answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent auditors verify a fraudulent claim. One operator can still create a hundred identities, but each must tie up capital and each detected lie destroys part of it; splitting an account does not multiply influence for free. The audit rule might compare ferrous shipments, orchard yields, and quartz invoices against signed delivery records, making fabricated identities costly to maintain and risky to use.
